#### 25.5 Cross-cutting design rules

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| **DB-01** | **Every table** carries `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`, `created_by_user_id BIGINT NOT NULL`, `updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ`, `updated_by_user_id BIGINT`. These are set by the application service layer, never left to the caller, and never editable through a screen. | [MUST] |
| **DB-02** | **Delete policy. There are no hard deletes in any `txn_` table, in `sys_audit_log`, in `sys_state_transition`, in `txn_custody_event`, or in `txn_observation`.** The application's database login is granted no DELETE permission on those tables. Withdrawal, cancellation, rejection and abortion are **states**, each with a mandatory reason. Master tables may carry `is_active` and, for genuinely wrong entries never used, `is_deleted BOOLEAN` plus `deleted_at`, `deleted_by_user_id`, `delete_reason`; deletion is refused if the master row is referenced anywhere. A voided record remains queryable and printable, watermarked VOID. | [MUST] |
| **DB-03** | Nothing is ever removed to "clean up". Retention is handled by `sys_retention_policy` with a proposal, a named authoriser and a permanent disposal record. No scheduled job may issue a DELETE against a technical record. | [MUST] |
| **DB-04** | **The audit log design.** One table, `sys_audit_log`, written by **database triggers** on every audited table, so that a change made by any route — the application, a maintenance script, or a person with a database client — is recorded. Columns: `id BIGINT`, `unit_id`, `entity_type VARCHAR(40)`, `entity_id BIGINT`, `action VARCHAR(20)` (insert, update, delete-attempt, state_change, login, print, export, download, permission_denied, unblind), `field_name VARCHAR(60)`, `old_value TEXT`, `new_value TEXT`, `changed_by_user_id`, `changed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `reason_id`, `reason_text TEXT`, `ip_address VARCHAR(45)`, `session_id VARCHAR(60)`, `request_id VARCHAR(40)`, `source VARCHAR(20)` (application, script, direct), `row_hash CHAR(64) NOT NULL` — a SHA-256 taken over this row's own content together with the `row_hash` of the row before it, so the table forms a chain that the verification job of M21-31b re-computes end to end and can therefore prove that no row was altered or removed by any route. One row **per changed field**, not one per record, so that a change history reads as a list of specific changes. Indexes: `(entity_type, entity_id, changed_at)`, `(changed_by_user_id, changed_at)`, `(changed_at)`. Partitioned or archived by month once it grows. **Privileges, per M21-31: the application's database account has INSERT and SELECT only. UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, ALTER and DROP are revoked, together with the right to create, alter, disable or drop a trigger on the table, and the audit tables are owned by a separate database account that the application cannot authenticate as.** A guard trigger raises an error on every such operation a trigger can intercept and writes a `delete-attempt` row naming the account and the statement, so a blocked attempt is itself evidence; the operations no trigger can intercept are prevented by the grant model and the ownership, and the refusal surfaces through the database error log in the daily health digest (ARC-35). `reason_text` or `reason_id` is **NOT NULL for updates to** raw readings, results, methods, equipment status, competency authorisations, rate cards and any numbered document. | [MUST] |
| **DB-05** | The application sets the current user identity in a database session variable at the start of every request, so triggers can record `changed_by_user_id` without the application passing it into every statement. A write with no session user set is refused. Exactly one reserved non-interactive principal exists: the **scheduler account**. It has its own database role, its own `sys_user` row with `is_service_account = true`, `personnel_id` NULL, no password and no interactive login, and it cannot be granted any role that authorises, verifies, signs or issues. Scheduled jobs and the queue worker set the session user to that account, so their writes satisfy DB-01 and are attributed in `sys_audit_log` with `source = 'script'`. Any other connection that writes with no session user set is refused and the refusal is written to the database error log, which the daily health digest (ARC-35) surfaces. | [MUST] |
| **DB-06** | **The revision pattern for results.** `txn_result` holds one current row per (test, parameter) enforced by a partial unique index on `is_current`. Every change writes a `txn_result_revision` row holding the old and new values, the actor, the time and a mandatory reason, and increments `rev_no`. The raw readings in `txn_observation` are never updated: a correction is a **new observation row** whose `supersedes_observation_id` points at the old one, and the old one gets `is_excluded = true` with a reason. Both remain visible. | [MUST] |
| **DB-07** | **The revision pattern for reports.** An issued report row and its stored file are append-only. A correction is either an **amendment** (a new report row with `amends_report_id` set, carrying the literal statement "Amendment to Report, serial number X") or a **replacement** (a new report row with `supersedes_report_id` set, and the old row's `superseded_by_report_id` set). The original row is never updated except to set `superseded_by_report_id` and `state`, and those two updates are the only ones the database permits, enforced by a trigger. A machine-generated change list between the two versions is stored and printable. | [MUST] |
| **DB-08** | **Numbering: how to stop two clerks getting the same number.** The counter lives in `mst_numbering_counter`, one row per unit, document type, period and scope. Allocation runs in **its own short transaction**: lock the single counter row (`SELECT last_number FROM mst_numbering_counter WHERE ... FOR UPDATE`), increment it, commit. The number is then used in the business transaction. Because the counter row is locked, a second clerk's request waits a few milliseconds and gets the next number. **The following are forbidden and must not appear in the code:** `SELECT MAX(number) + 1` (two clerks read the same maximum and both get the same number); a database sequence (sequences leak numbers on rollback, and cannot be reset per financial year under control); generating any number in the browser or on a tablet. If the business transaction that was to consume the number fails, is abandoned or is lost to a server restart, the number is not reused: a `sys_number_void` row is written with reason `allocation not completed`. A reconciliation job runs at server start-up and nightly, finds every number at or below `last_number` with neither a document row nor a `sys_number_void` row, writes that row automatically, and records its outcome in `sys_job_run`. The Series Register therefore reports Missing only for a real defect, and the alert of DB-10 stays meaningful. | [MUST] |
| **DB-09** | **Numbers are allotted at the moment of issue, immediately before the transaction that commits the document, by the mechanism of DB-08 — never when a user opens a "new" form.** Otherwise abandoned drafts consume numbers. A draft shows "Not yet numbered". | [MUST] |
| **DB-10** | An allotted number is **never reused**. If a document is cancelled, its number is retired and a row is written to `sys_number_void` recording who voided it and why. A **series register report** lists every number from 1 to the current counter with its state — issued, cancelled, or **missing** — and any "missing" row raises an alert, because it means a bug. This is the software form of the General Financial Rules requirement to account for every form in a receipt book. | [MUST] |
| **DB-11** | For tax documents, the series definition enforces the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, rule 46(b): at most **16 characters**, only letters, digits, hyphen and slash, consecutive, unique for the financial year. The system **refuses to save a series definition whose maximum possible number would exceed 16 characters.** Sample numbers, report numbers and Unique Laboratory Report numbers are not tax documents and are not subject to the 16-character limit. | [MUST] |
| **DB-12** | The financial year for a number is derived from the **India Standard Time date**, not the stored Coordinated Universal Time date. A document created at 04:00 IST on 1 April is 22:30 UTC on 31 March, and must land in the new financial year. This is a real and easily missed defect. | [MUST] |
| **DB-13** | The Unique Laboratory Report number is produced by a **template engine reading `mst_ulr_config`**, never by joining strings in code, because the format changed in June 2026 and the unit may be mid-transition. The running number is per calendar year, allotted atomically by the same mechanism as DB-08, and **only at the moment of report authorisation.** A draft report has no such number. | [MUST] |
| **DB-14** | **Attachments are files on disk or in object storage, with metadata in `sys_attachment`. Binary content is never stored inside a database row.** The reasons: photographs at 15 GB a year would make the database backup unusably slow and the restore-time objective unachievable; a database restore would then be an all-or-nothing operation; and streaming a 5 MB PDF out of a table wastes memory on a 16 GB server. Path layout: `/<unit>/<year>/<month>/<entity_type>/<id>/<uuid>.<ext>`. The stored name is a generated identifier, never the user's file name. Every attachment stores a SHA-256 fingerprint, verified weekly (NFR-42); where a derived long-term-validation copy of a report exists (NFR-121) it is a separate `sys_attachment` row with its own fingerprint and is verified as an independent row, and only the issued original is ever served to a customer or compared by the public file-check. **`pdf_sha256` is taken over the final stored bytes of the issued file, including any embedded signature** — the checksum is computed after signing, not before, so the weekly job re-computes the same value for the life of the record. Issued report files are marked immutable and the file permissions are set read-only. **The backup procedure must cover the file store and the database together, and the restore drill must verify a report PDF opens after restore.** | [MUST] |
| **DB-15** | **State machines.** Each transaction table holds `state VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL`, `state_changed_at TIMESTAMPTZ`, `state_changed_by_user_id`. Allowed moves live in `sys_state_transition_rule` as data. Every move is executed by **one service function** which: checks the rule exists, checks the actor's permission, checks a reason where required, checks the "must be a different person" rule where required, updates the state columns, writes a `sys_state_transition` row with the seconds spent in the previous state, and runs the configured side effects. **No screen, controller or report may set a state column directly.** Turnaround, bottleneck and hold-duration reporting all read `sys_state_transition`, never scattered timestamps. | [MUST] |
| **DB-16** | **Multi-unit readiness from day one.** `unit_id BIGINT NOT NULL` appears on every transaction table and on masters that can vary by unit. It forms part of the unique key for every number series. Every query passes through a mandatory unit scope supplied by the session, and a test confirms that a user of one unit cannot read another unit's records even by supplying an identifier directly. There is exactly one narrow exception, for WF-20's inter-unit referral: a row whose `performing_unit_id` or `billing_unit_id` names the session unit is visible to that unit through the **inter-unit referral views only**, which expose the sample identity, test, method, result and price — not the customer identity, the audit trail or the invoice. All other queries remain scoped to `unit_id` alone. The exception is declared as named views rather than as a row predicate, because `txn_observation`, `txn_result`, `txn_verification` and `sys_state_transition` carry no unit column and are reached by join. This costs almost nothing now and is a rewrite later if omitted. | [MUST] |
| **DB-17** | **Time.** All moments are stored as Coordinated Universal Time in `TIMESTAMPTZ` (or `DATETIME(3)` set to UTC). The application timezone is `Asia/Kolkata`, which is UTC plus 5 hours 30 minutes with no daylight saving. Display is always India Standard Time. Calendar dates that are dates in law or in trade — report date, invoice date, calibration due date, expiry date, retention date — are stored as `DATE` in India Standard Time terms, not derived from a UTC timestamp. Every "today" comparison uses the India Standard Time date. | [MUST] |
| **DB-18** | **Money and quantities.** Money is `DECIMAL(14,2)`. Tax percentages are `DECIMAL(6,3)`. Quantities are `DECIMAL(18,6)`. Measured and reported values are `DECIMAL(18,6)`; the full-precision computed value before rounding is `DECIMAL(24,10)`. **Floating-point types are forbidden for money and for reported results**, because they cannot represent decimal values exactly and the same calculation can then give two different answers. Rounding happens **once**, at result finalisation, using the method's stored rounding rule, and both the unrounded and the presented value are stored, with the number of decimals used. | [MUST] |
| **DB-19** | **Storing "less than the detection limit" and "not tested".** `txn_result` holds three related columns: `value_num` (the number, if there is one), `value_text` (a descriptive result such as a grade or "Absent"), and `value_qualifier` from a fixed list: `=` (a plain value), `<` (less than), `>` (greater than), `ND` (not detected), `NT` (not tested), `NP` (not performed), `IS` (insufficient sample), `PRES` / `ABS` (present / absent). Where the qualifier is `<` or `>`, `value_num` holds the limit and `detection_limit` holds the method's limit of detection. Rules: **never store `<0.5` as text in a numeric column** (it stops all averaging and trending); **never store 0 for "not detected"** (it silently corrupts every average, trend and grade calculation); **never leave a not-tested parameter as an empty row that looks like a missing entry** — say so explicitly with `NT` and a reason. Display is generated from the qualifier and the value: "< 0.5 %", "Not detected (limit of detection 0.1 %)", "Not tested". Statistical functions and the grading engine must handle each qualifier explicitly and refuse to guess. | [MUST] |
| **DB-20** | Every result row stores `method_id` **and** `method_revision`, and every observation stores `equipment_id` and, where the method consumes one, `consumable_lot_id` or `prepared_solution_id`. These links are what make the retrospective impact analysis of a failed instrument, a bad reagent lot or a wrongly standardised working solution a single query rather than an impossible manual search, and the prepared-solution path reaches its own source lots through `mst_prepared_solution_source` (M12-32). **They are `NOT NULL` where the method requires them**, and where the method consumes a reagent exactly one of the two consumption columns is set. | [MUST] |
| **DB-21** | Snapshot rules. `txn_sample_test` snapshots the method, its revision, the standard turnaround and the price at the moment the test is created. `txn_report_test.snapshot_json` freezes every value that is printed and, per result, the `txn_result.id` and the `rev_no` that value came from — the revision number is not a printed value, so it must be frozen explicitly or DB-43 has nothing to compare against. `txn_report` snapshots the printed customer name and address. A report reprinted in 2033 must render identically even if the method, the price and the customer's address have all changed since. | [MUST] |
| **DB-22** | Reference data that changes over time is dated, never overwritten: rate cards, tax rates, specification and grade tables, methods, competency authorisations, accredited scope, statements, templates, retention policies. Each has `effective_from` and `effective_to`, and every historical query selects the row in force on the relevant date. Overlapping ranges are refused. | [MUST] |
| **DB-23** | Character encoding is UTF-8 throughout — database, connection, application and PDF — so that Telugu and Devanagari text survives from the screen to the printed report. This is set once, at creation, and verified with real Telugu test data in Phase 1. | [MUST] |
| **DB-24** | The database schema is created and changed only by numbered forward-only migration scripts held in source control (ARC-29). The production schema is never edited by hand. | [MUST] |

#### 25.6 The most important integrity rules, as constraints and triggers

These are the rules that stop impossible data from existing at all. Each is implemented in the database, not only in the application, because an application bug or a maintenance script must not be able to break them.

| ID | Rule | How it is enforced |
|---|---|---|
| DB-25 | An issued report cannot be modified, except to set `superseded_by_report_id` and `state`. | Trigger on `txn_report` that raises an error on any other column change where `state` is issued or later. |
| DB-26 | An issued report always has a stored file and a fingerprint. | `CHECK (state <> 'ISSUED' OR (pdf_attachment_id IS NOT NULL AND pdf_sha256 IS NOT NULL))`. |
| DB-27 | A report carrying a Unique Laboratory Report number or the accreditation symbol contains no out-of-scope parameter. | `CHECK ((ulr_no IS NULL AND nabl_symbol_used = false) OR contains_out_of_scope = false)`. |
| DB-28 | A result cannot be verified by the person who submitted it, unless an override with a reason has been recorded. | Trigger on `txn_verification` comparing `actor_personnel_id` with the test's `submitted_by_personnel_id`; an override requires a linked reason and raises a nonconformity. |
| DB-29 | A test cannot move to submitted while any mandatory parameter has no result row. | Trigger on the state transition, called from the single transition function. |
| DB-30 | An observation cannot be recorded against equipment whose calibration or intermediate check had expired at `observed_at`. | Trigger comparing `observed_at` against the equipment's valid-until dates; an override requires an authorised user, a reason, and raises a nonconformity. |
| DB-31 | An observation cannot consume a consumable lot that was expired, rejected or unapproved at `observed_at`. | Trigger with the same override pattern. |
| DB-32 | An observation cannot be recorded by a person without a valid authorisation for that method and the "perform" activity on `observed_at`. | Trigger against `mst_competency`; same override pattern. |
| DB-33 | A raw observation row can never be updated or deleted; a correction is a new row. | No UPDATE or DELETE permission on `txn_observation` for the application login, except a single permitted update setting `is_excluded` with a reason. |
| DB-34 | Exactly one current result exists per test and parameter. | Partial unique index on `(sample_test_id, parameter_id)` where `is_current` is true. |
| DB-35 | A number series never issues the same number twice for a unit, document type and period. | Unique constraint on the resulting document number column, plus the locked-counter allocation of DB-08. |
| DB-36 | An invoice cannot be cancelled after the return period in which it was reported has been filed; the correction must be a credit note. | Trigger comparing `doc_date` against the filed-up-to date, which is held per tax registration and per return period in `sys_setting` (scope `gst_registration`, key `returns_filed_upto`), not as a single column on `mst_gst_registration`. |
| DB-37 | A receipt's allocations cannot exceed the receipt amount, and an invoice's paid amount cannot exceed its total. | `CHECK (paid_amount <= total_amount)` plus a trigger summing `txn_receipt_allocation` (over both invoice and order allocations) against `txn_receipt.amount`. |
| DB-38 | A sample cannot be disposed of before its retention date, and only with a recorded authorisation. | `CHECK (disposed_at IS NULL OR disposal_authorised_by IS NOT NULL)` plus a trigger comparing against `retain_until`. |
| DB-39 | A complaint cannot be closed by a person in the involvement set of the work complained about, as defined in M15-20. | Trigger over the signature records, the observation and result authorship columns, the custody events, the `sys_state_transition` rows for the related sample, test, report and invoice, and the unblind-approval records. `sys_audit_log` rows whose action is print, export, login, download or permission denial are excluded from the test, because merely having read or printed the work does not make a person a party to it. |
| DB-40 | A refund voucher must reference the receipt voucher it reverses, as rule 51 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules requires. | `CHECK (doc_type <> 'REFUND_VOUCHER' OR receipt_voucher_id IS NOT NULL)`, with a foreign key. |
| DB-41 | Every transaction row is *owned* by exactly one unit. Where WF-20 applies, the performing and billing units are recorded separately in `txn_sample_test.performing_unit_id` and `txn_order.billing_unit_id`; both default to the owning unit. | `unit_id NOT NULL` with a foreign key on every `txn_` table; the two referral columns are nullable with foreign keys to `mst_unit`. |
| DB-42 | A test whose quality-control run failed cannot be reported until the breach has been dispositioned. | Trigger on the report-issue transition, checking `txn_qc_affected_test` for an open breach. |
| DB-43 | A report cannot move to Authorised or to Issued if any allocation it covers is not in state Verified at that moment, or if any of that allocation's current results carries a `rev_no` higher than the one frozen in `txn_report_test.snapshot_json`. | Trigger on both the report-authorisation and the report-issue transitions, re-reading `txn_sample_test.state` and `txn_result.rev_no` (where `is_current`) for every row of `txn_report_test`, and raising an error naming the offending allocation and its report number. The authorisation checkpoint is the load-bearing one, because the report number, the Unique Laboratory Report number, the rendered file, the checksum and the signature are all produced at authorisation. |
| DB-44 | A test caught in an open impact analysis cannot be verified or reported until it has been dispositioned. | Trigger on the verification and the report-issue transitions, checking `txn_ncr_affected` for a row against that test whose `disposition` is not set, and raising an error naming the nonconformity number. This is the database half of the withholding required by M11-24(g) and M12-12, and it complements DB-42, which covers a failed quality-control run rather than an impact analysis. |
| DB-45 | A report of type CONDITIONING cannot reach Issued without a completed conditioning lot behind it. | Trigger on the report-issue transition: where `report_type` is CONDITIONING there must be exactly one `txn_conditioning_lot` row whose `report_id` is this report, whose `conditioned_mass` and `moisture_pct` are both set, and whose `txn_conditioning_bale` row count equals `declared_no_of_bales`; otherwise the issue is refused naming which of the three is missing. |
| DB-46 | The stock figure is never typed. `txn_stock_ledger` is append-only, `mst_consumable_lot.qty_on_hand` is maintained only by trigger from it, and no lot's balance can go below zero. | No UPDATE or DELETE permission on `txn_stock_ledger` for the application login; a trigger on insert recomputes `qty_on_hand` and writes `balance_after`; `CHECK (qty_on_hand >= 0)` on `mst_consumable_lot` and `CHECK (balance_after >= 0)` on the ledger, which is the database half of M12-14. A physical-count adjustment reaches the ledger only through an approved `txn_stock_verification_line`, enforced by a trigger requiring `approved_by_personnel_id` on the parent run (M12-18). |

### 26. Implementation plan and phasing

**Assumption for every effort figure: one full-time developer, working alone, five days a week.** Figures are in developer-weeks and include design, coding, automated tests, the developer's own testing, and writing the documentation for that phase. They do **not** include the laboratory's user acceptance testing time, which runs in parallel and needs the laboratory's people, not the developer's.

If the developer is part-time, multiply the calendar duration accordingly and do not compress the phases — the sequence matters more than the speed.

#### 26.1 Phase summary

| Phase | Goal | Effort (developer-weeks, range) | Cumulative (weeks) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0** | Understand the real process; freeze the open questions; load the master data | 2 | 2 |
| **1** | Replace the paper sample register end to end, from the reviewed Test Request to a signed report with a QR code, including the conditioned-mass certificate of the conditioning module (M10), the equipment, lot, competency and environment capture that gates a result, and report amendment and withdrawal | 32–38 | 34–40 |
| **2** | Money: rate cards, enquiry and quotation, invoices, receipts, payment holds, statutory returns | 7–9 | 41–49 |
| **3** | Equipment lifecycle, stock economics and impact analysis: the calibration programme, the traceability chain, the stock ledger, supplier evaluation, training records, and the out-of-calibration impact analysis | 4–6 | 45–55 |
| **4** | Quality system: nonconforming work, complaints, corrective action, quality control, proficiency testing, accredited scope, decision rules and statements of conformity, document control | 7–9 | 52–64 |
| **5** | Outward-facing: customer portal, notifications, dashboards, analytics, public verification hardening | 6–8 | 58–72 |
| **6** | Depth: instrument file import, stronger digital signing, worksheets, subcontracting, second unit readiness | 5–7 | 63–79 |

Roughly **fifteen to eighteen months of one person's full time** to a complete system, with the paper sample register replaced somewhere in **month eight or nine**.

**How to read these figures, honestly.** They are ranges, not commitments, and the range is the point: a solo developer building around twenty-five dated master tables, a data-driven state machine, a field-level trigger audit trail, an author-it-yourself calculation and grading engine, tagged and signed PDFs with Indic text, a separately hosted accessible verification service, four manuals and the ISO/IEC 17025 clause 7.11.2 validation package cannot be costed to the week. The figures **exclude** leave and public holidays, the defect-fix cycles that follow each user acceptance test, and the laboratory's own master-data work (the test catalogue of PLN-08, the specification and grade tables, the rate cards, the equipment and competency records) — that work is owned by the laboratory and runs on its own clock. Three items carry most of the schedule risk and should be attacked first, inside Phase 1, not left to the end: (a) the tagged and digitally signed PDF with correct Telugu and Devanagari shaping — the library choice is now made and tested (§24.4), but the structure tree is hand-built, so the very first template must be written tag-first and no later pass can retrofit it (NFR-70, NFR-93, ARC-17, PLN-28); (b) the calculation and grading engine a non-programmer must be able to author (NFR-109, AC-38); and (c) the trigger-written audit trail with the revoked-DELETE grant model (DB-04, DB-05, NFR-43), which must be in continuous integration from day one because retrofitting it across forty tables is not practical.

Phase 1 is large because it is the release that goes live, and everything an issued certificate depends on has to be inside it. It is delivered in internal increments in this order — masters, then intake and acceptance against a reviewed request, then the bench with its equipment, lot, competency and environment gates, then verification, then the report with its amendment and withdrawal paths — but it has **one** go-live, one acceptance milestone and one cut-over, described in §26.3.

---

#### 26.2 Phase 0 — Sit in the laboratory (2 weeks)

| ID | Item |
|---|---|
| **PLN-01** | **A two-day sit-in at Dharmavaram**, at the counter and at the bench, watching the real process from a sample arriving to a report leaving. Not a meeting. The developer writes down, minute by minute, what the clerk does, what the tester does, what they write on, what they carry, and what they shout across the room. [MUST] |
| **PLN-02** | **Collect a physical copy of every existing form, register, worksheet and issued document**: the sample receipt slip, the intake register, every result worksheet in use, a Limited Test report, a Grading Certificate, a conditioned-mass report, a money receipt, a tax invoice, the monthly return sent to CSTRI headquarters, the annual return, the calibration register, the stock register, and the daily collection register. Photograph or scan every one. **Nothing in the report or register design is guessed while a real specimen exists.** [MUST] |
| **PLN-03** | Walk through the ten site-survey questions of §9.2 of the research brief: staff count, computers, network, power, internet, printers, which instruments have a digital output, samples per day in peak and off season, who signs, and how reports are delivered. [MUST] |
| **PLN-04** | **Confirm the open-question list** (§28 and the other sections' lists) with the Unit Incharge in one sitting, and record the answer or the agreed default for each. Anything still open after this session is escalated in writing. [MUST] |
| **PLN-05** | Extract at least **20 completed historical worksheets with their hand-calculated results**, to be used as the calculation regression suite of NFR-41. These are the single most valuable artefact of Phase 0. [MUST] |
| **PLN-06** | Obtain, in writing: the tax registration the unit bills under and a sample tax invoice; the current approved rate card; the list of authorised signatories with their disciplines; the quality manual's rules on amendments and record retention; and the accreditation position of the unit. [MUST] |
| **PLN-07** | The task recorded here — determining an external accounting system's language, framework, database and integration surface — is **withdrawn**: the unit runs no such system, so there is nothing to determine and nothing to build inside (ARC-13, ARC-14). In its place: get that confirmed in writing by the Unit Incharge, and record how the unit's accounts wing keeps the money records today — which books and registers the money passes through, how invoice and receipt numbers are allocated in them, and who does that work. Phase 2 must issue invoices and receipts that do not collide with numbers those books already carry (OPEN-Q-T15), and it allocates them itself, because the laboratory system owns its customer master, its invoice numbering and its stock records (M22-17). [MUST] |
| **PLN-08** | Build the **test catalogue as a spreadsheet**: every test, method, standard and year, parameters, units, reading counts, formulae, rounding, minimum quantity, turnaround, price, accredited or not. This is master-data work, not coding, and it is the most under-estimated task in every laboratory system project. Give it a named owner in the laboratory and a deadline. [MUST] |
| **PLN-09** | Set up the repository, the three environments, the build, the database migration mechanism, and the low-specification reference machine. [MUST] |
| **PLN-28** | **The Indic text and tagged-PDF acceptance test. It is written, it is in the build, and it passes: conformance is now demonstrated rather than assumed.** It was written before the document component's layout code, as this item always required, which is why the defects it found cost about a day instead of a rewrite. It renders a single page carrying ప్రయోగశాల, శ్రీ ధర్మవరం, కీర్తి, మూర్తి, ప్రు, పట్టు and केंद्रीय रेशम बोर्ड — English, Telugu and Devanagari together on one page, because that is what an issued certificate carries, and a test page carrying only one script hides a whole class of defect — and asserts four things: that rendering throws no exception; that the glyph identifiers and advances written into the page's content stream are exactly what harfbuzzjs returns for the same string in the same font, held as a golden file so that a change in shaping is visible rather than silent; that every one of those strings is found, in logical order, by a plain text search of the text extracted back out of the finished file; and that `veraPDF -f ua1` passes that file with no failed rule. It then applies the digital signature to the same file and runs all four assertions again against the signed file, adding a check that the signature's byte range still covers the whole document. Signing is an **incremental update**: it appends to the file rather than rewriting it, so a validator run made before signing says nothing about the document a customer actually receives, and only the signed run is evidence. **The measured result, on the built document component: veraPDF 1.30.2, profile ua1, 106 of 106 rules, `isCompliant="true"` — unsigned and signed alike.** The reason this test stays in the build for the life of the system is recorded here, where a developer looking to make the build faster will read it. This specification, following the wider literature, carried the claim that the layout library passes PDF/UA-1. Run against our own document it did not: it failed four rules across twenty-five checks, and repairing those four exposed two further failures that are only reachable once the first four are gone. Six defects, then, sat between a document that already had a complete structure tree, correct `/ActualText` and byte-perfect shaping — everything ARC-47 asks for, checked in the emitted file rather than assumed — and a document that actually conforms. Not one of the six shows on the printed page, and not one of them was going to be found by reading the code; they were found by running the validator over a file everybody believed was finished. Each is now recorded as its own requirement in §24.4 and is not restated here; one of them is ARC-49, which this run confirms is real and whose workaround it confirms works. The default shaping engine **throws** on ordinary Telugu rather than mis-setting it, so the failure is a crashed report, not an ugly one — which is why the shaping engine is a named, deliberate choice in §24.4 rather than whatever the layout library ships with. The text layer is built after shaping and so comes out in **visual** rather than logical order, which leaves the certificate unsearchable, uncopyable and read aloud in the wrong character order — the substance of NFR-70 and NFR-93, not a cosmetic detail — and no accessibility validator detects it. And a font-subset side table that the format does not require can fail validation for one typeface while another passes, so the build looks healthy until somebody changes the font. This one test is also the only thing that will catch any of these coming back from a dependency upgrade in five years' time, made by someone who is not this developer. Pin the exact versions it was written against — pdfkit 0.19.1, harfbuzzjs 1.6.0 and veraPDF 1.30.2 — name them beside the test, and vendor them offline per ARC-16. **The validator is a build-machine tool and belongs nowhere else** — the development machine and the ARC-30 continuous integration job, never the laboratory server, for the reason ARC-53 records. It cost about a day, inside PLN-09's setup week. [MUST] |

**What the laboratory can do at the end:** nothing new in software — but the specification is now anchored to real documents and real numbers rather than to assumptions.
**Acceptance milestone:** a signed-off open-question register, a signed-off test catalogue spreadsheet, the 20 regression worksheets in hand, and the PLN-28 text-and-tagging test running green in the build.
**Risk if skipped:** the data model is wrong. Specifically, "what is a sample" for a conditioning lot, and how many identifiers exist, cannot be answered from a description; they can only be answered by looking at the paper. Getting this wrong is discovered in month four and costs a rebuild.

#### 26.3 Phase 1 — The first usable release (32–38 weeks)

**Goal: on the day this goes live, the paper sample register stops being the primary record.** That is why this phase, and not billing, comes first: the register is the thing the staff touch forty-six times a day.

**Included:** unit, customer, customer category and contact masters; sample type, silk variety, reeling device masters; test, method, parameter, unit-of-measure, specification and grade masters; numbering series; the Unique Laboratory Report number configuration engine, which DB-13 and AC-05 require from the first issued report; the Test Request record with the customer and sender, the requested tests per sample with the method choice, the agreed specification set and the sample-handling and return terms (M3-05 to M3-09); the Request Review record with the per-test capability check of WF-2 stored as a printable record, not merely displayed (M3-13, using the check logic of M2-06 and M2-07); and the walk-in path of WF-31, which creates the request shell at the counter and forces the review before acceptance (WF-1, M2-23) — the `decision_rule_id` and per-parameter conformity fields exist on the request from Phase 1 but are deliberately left unused until Phase 4; roles, permissions and users; the staff register separate from the login account (M13-01, M13-02); the authorisation matrix with enforcement evaluated against the date of the action on allocate, submit, check, verify and sign (M13-07, M13-08, M13-09, as WF-62, WF-76 and DB-32 already require), with provisional authorisation per M13.5 rule 3 where no assessment record yet exists; the segregation-of-duties rule with the recorded, counted override (M13-10); the Authorised Signatory Register and the per-parameter signatory coverage check including the hold where no signatory covers a parameter (M13-11, M13-12, M7-25, M7-26, M7-35); the Delegation Register (M13-13, M13-14, M7-31 to M7-33); the as-at-date authorisation query (M13-16); sample registration including batch registration; label printing; sample acceptance and rejection with a condition checklist and photographs; sub-sample creation; the Sampling Record for samples the laboratory draws itself, with the sampling-plan reference held as a text reference in this phase (M4-35); allocation per test to a tester; the result-entry screen with raw readings, statistics and the calculation engine; the grading engine; the conditioning lot and its conditioned-mass certificate (M10) — the bale set with its per-bale weighings, the moisture set drawn from it, the append-only dry-weighing series to constant mass, and the conditioned-mass computation against the conditioning method's stored numeric constants — issued as a report type through the same numbering, authorisation, signature and QR path as a test report (DB-45); the equipment master with its method links, criticality, state machine, calibration and intermediate-check schedule, calibration and check events with certificate files and stored correction factors applied by the calculation engine, and the hard block with reasoned, nonconformity-raising override at allocation and at result entry, plus the mandatory equipment reference on every observation and the usage log (M11-01 to M11-20, M11-25, M11-26, and M11-30 for the standard weights and photograph sets the checks are made against); the item and batch master with expiry, open shelf life, lot acceptance out of quarantine, per-observation consumption capture and the block evaluated against the observation date with its override (M12-01 to M12-11); manual temperature and humidity capture with per-area and per-method limits, the reading schedule and missed-reading marker, the excursion and withheld-test records, the environment link on every result, and the pre-conditioning gate with its effect on the promised date (M16-01 to M16-13); verification with send-back; report generation with the frozen PDF, the fingerprint, the QR code and the internal electronic signature; the append-only issued-report file; report amendment and replacement as first-class documents, each with a mandatory reason code, the machine-generated change manifest, the recorded lineage and the SUPERSEDED watermark, the numbering rule for re-issues, and the automatic nonconforming-work record; report withdrawal with its recall record and its logged customer notification; a new verification token per version, with the old token reporting GENUINE — SUPERSEDED and naming the replacement (M8-50 to M8-60, M9-11); a minimal nonconforming-work record sufficient to satisfy M8-58 and M8-59; the public verification service; sample retention, return and disposal; chain of custody and scan stations; the audit trail; the state-transition ledger; turnaround dates with the working calendar; the sample register and test register; and full export.

**Requirement identifiers from this section that must be satisfied:** NFR-01 to NFR-05, NFR-06, NFR-11 to NFR-19, NFR-27 to NFR-36, NFR-37 to NFR-44, NFR-45 to NFR-58, NFR-68 to NFR-72, NFR-73 to NFR-78, NFR-79 to NFR-87, NFR-88, NFR-89, NFR-92 to NFR-94, NFR-95 to NFR-101, NFR-102 to NFR-107, NFR-109 to NFR-112, NFR-116 to NFR-120; ARC-01 to ARC-12, ARC-14, ARC-15, ARC-16 to ARC-32, ARC-33 to ARC-53; DB-01 to DB-26, DB-28 to DB-35, DB-38, DB-41, DB-43, DB-45.

ARC-13 is the single architecture rule Phase 1 does not have to satisfy, because it is not operative: there is no accounting package to build inside, and the rule becomes live only if somebody proposes one. ARC-14 and ARC-15 are in the list because they are the operative pair — the system owns its own customer master, numbering, invoices, receipts and stock outright, and it is not built on a proprietary managed service — and both bind from the first release.

The database rules deliberately excluded are those whose tables arrive later: DB-36, DB-37 and DB-40 with the invoice, receipt-allocation and refund-voucher tables in Phase 2; DB-44 and DB-46 with the impact-analysis records and the stock ledger in Phase 3; and DB-27, DB-39 and DB-42 with the accredited-scope master, the complaint register and the quality-control tables in Phase 4. Two further boundaries: NFR-68's **recorded** accessibility conformance audit and the public service's security review are completed in Phase 5 (§26.7), so Phase 1 builds the verification page to that standard and may, under go-live checklist item 12, go live with the page deliberately deferred; and NFR-121 binds only if a trusted timestamp is ever applied at all, which under the OPEN-Q-T31 default it is not — the rule is kept dormant rather than dropped, and §23.5 records what would bring it back.

**What the laboratory can do at the end:** receive a sample at the counter and hand over an acknowledgement slip; record the Test Request and its review, with the per-test capability check, before the sample is accepted; print a label; accept or reject with a recorded reason; allocate the test; enter twenty readings from the keyboard; be refused when the instrument is out of calibration, the reagent lot has expired, the tester is not authorised or the conditioning has not been done, and record who overrode it and why; have the average, deviation and grade computed; verify the result as a second person; issue a numbered, signed report with a working QR code; amend or withdraw that report properly if it is wrong; print it; find any sample or report by number, customer or date; and produce the sample register for the month.

**Acceptance milestone:** the laboratory processes **one full day's real intake** through the system in parallel with paper, produces every report for that day from the system, and a member of the public scans one of those reports' QR codes on a phone and sees the correct status. Then attempt to accept a sample against a request still in Pending Review, and confirm the refusal names the missing review (WF-1). Then amend one of that day's reports, re-scan the original QR code, and confirm the page reports GENUINE — SUPERSEDED and names the replacement (AC-22, AC-23). Then confirm that a signatory authorised for only one discipline is refused when signing a report carrying a parameter outside that discipline, the system naming the parameter (M7-25, M13-12). Plus: the cable-pull day (NFR-27) and the calculation regression suite (NFR-41) both pass.

**Risk if skipped or reordered:** if billing goes first, the staff get a system that adds work at the counter and removes none at the bench, they keep the paper register, and once a parallel register exists the software's data goes stale and the project is effectively over. If the request review, the equipment and lot gates, the competency matrix or the amendment path are pushed out of this phase, the release that replaces the paper register issues certificates it cannot stand behind: samples accepted with no reviewed request, results recorded against instruments with no calibration record, and a wrong certificate correctable only by re-typing it under the same number.

---

#### 26.4 Phase 2 — Money and statutory returns (7–9 weeks)

**Included:** enquiry and quotation; the pricing of an accepted request from the rate card, with priority multipliers and the total carried on the request; rate cards with customer-class and method-based pricing, minimum quantities, per-unit and per-point charges, priority multipliers and the express-service rules; tax master with treatments and dated rates; tax registration master and the intra-state versus inter-state decision; the five document types (receipt voucher, tax invoice, bill of supply, credit and debit note, refund voucher) each with its own financial-year series; the separate money receipt; payments in all modes with the flexible reference table; the awaiting-credit worklist and provisional release; bank statement and payment-portal import, recorded as an import batch with duplicate detection so a re-run cannot receipt the same line twice, and the matching screen for the unmatched lines; the customer running account; payment hold as an explicit state with an authorised, logged override that does not count against turnaround; the daily collection and remittance reconciliation report; **the monthly return to CSTRI headquarters, stored as an immutable snapshot when submitted**; the annual consolidated return; receivables ageing; the zero-charge advisory order type for in-house research and sub-unit samples; and the fields needed for Invoice Reference Number reporting left ready but not yet connected.

**Requirement identifiers from this section that must be satisfied:** DB-36, DB-37, DB-40, whose tables this phase creates.

**What the laboratory can do at the end:** quote for work and convert an accepted quotation into a priced request; bill correctly for any customer class and any priority; issue and reconcile receipts; hold work for payment visibly and lawfully; and produce the monthly return to headquarters in one click instead of retyping it from registers.

**Acceptance milestone:** one full month is billed and reconciled entirely in the system, the collection register balances against the bank, and the monthly return produced by the system matches the one the unit prepared by hand for the same month, line for line.

**Risk if skipped:** the laboratory keeps two systems, one for work and one for money, and the "revenue per test" question — which is what justifies equipment purchases and rate revisions to headquarters — stays unanswerable.

---

#### 26.5 Phase 3 — Equipment lifecycle, stock economics and impact analysis (4–6 weeks)

This phase **extends** the equipment, lot, competency and environment records that Phase 1 already built and gates results against. Nothing here is re-introduced; everything here reads or lengthens Phase 1 data.

**Included:** the equipment master extended to the full record set including software and firmware versions, ownership, range and least count; the typed equipment event table extended to maintenance, breakdown, repair and condemnation, with the equipment status label and the verification-before-return-to-service record (M11-21 to M11-23); the calibration programme extended with the planning view and the alert ladder; the metrological traceability route and the printable traceability-chain sheet carrying the calibrating laboratory's accreditation and scope (M11-10, M11-11); the annual maintenance contract register, the working asset record tab — supplier, purchase document, cost, date put to use, useful life, condemnation, with no depreciation or book-value field — and the annual physical verification (M11-27 to M11-29); the reference-standard class with its own calibration and re-verification cycle, as distinct from the standard weights and photograph sets that Phase 1 already registers for the intermediate checks; consumables and reference materials extended with the stock ledger, the reorder and expiry-alert economics, the prepared-solution register, and supplier evaluation with the approved supplier list; the competence evidence behind the authorisations already enforced since Phase 1 — documented competence requirements per function, qualification and experience records, training records, competence assessments, supervision records, periodic re-authorisation with the warn-then-suspend ladder, the accreditation-body notification task, confidentiality and impartiality undertakings, and the printable competence file (M13-03 to M13-06, M13-15, M13-17 to M13-25); the M13 authorisation check extended to the **SAMPLE** activity, which binds from this phase, so that only a person authorised to draw samples can be recorded as having drawn one; the environment chart and trend view; and **the retrospective impact-analysis screens** ("this instrument failed — list every test, sample and issued report that used it since the last good check") for equipment and for consumable lots, each disposition driving customer notification and report recall (M11-24, M12-12).

**Requirement identifiers from this section that must be satisfied:** DB-44 and DB-46, whose impact-analysis records and stock ledger this phase creates.

**What the laboratory can do at the end:** know what is due for calibration before it is overdue; show an assessor the traceability chain from a reading back to a national standard; answer the assessor's hardest question — which results a failed instrument or a bad reagent lot touched — in one click, and record what was decided about each; **evidence the competence behind each authorisation** the system has been enforcing since Phase 1; and manage stock, suppliers and training records in the same system as the work.

**Acceptance milestone:** deliberately fail one instrument's calibration in the system and produce the complete list of affected tests and reports, disposition each one as not-affected, retest, amend or withdraw-and-replace, and show the resulting nonconformity record and the customer notifications it drove. Then attempt to enter a result on that instrument and be refused (the block itself was accepted in Phase 1).

**Risk if skipped:** the mandatory evaluation of previous results after an equipment or reagent failure cannot be done at all, so "nobody can list the affected reports" survives go-live; the traceability chain has to be assembled by hand from certificates for every assessment; and stock, supplier and training records stay on paper.

---

#### 26.6 Phase 4 — The quality system (7–9 weeks)

**Included:** the accredited-scope master, the in-scope flag per test and the automatic split of a mixed order into an accredited report and a non-accredited report, extending the Unique Laboratory Report number configuration engine built in Phase 1; the statements master; the decision-rule master and the per-parameter statement of conformity; measurement uncertainty with its reporting policy; method verification and validation records gating a method version becoming active; deviations with their four gates; the nonconforming work register **extended** with risk level, impact analysis, recall and corrective action — Phase 1's minimal record, which M8-58 and M8-59 require the moment a report can be amended, is the thing this phase builds out; the complaint register with the independent-closure rule; quality-control plans, control charts with configurable rules, and **the withholding of release on a breach**; the proficiency-testing register and the two-year coverage plan against the accredited scope; document control with revisions and read-acknowledgement — at which point the sampling-plan reference held as text since Phase 1 becomes a controlled-document link, exactly as M4-35 is worded to degrade; internal audit; the management review data pack; and the risk register.

**Requirement identifiers from this section that must be satisfied:** DB-27, DB-39, DB-42, whose masters and registers this phase creates.

**What the laboratory can do at the end:** state conformity against a specification under a named decision rule; keep the accreditation claim on a report strictly inside the accredited scope; refuse to release results behind a failed control check; and walk an assessor through every register from the screen.

**Acceptance milestone:** issue an order that mixes one accredited parameter with one outside the scope, and confirm the system produces two separate reports, one carrying the symbol and the Unique Laboratory Report number and one carrying neither, with no asterisk or footnote used to distinguish scope. Then fail a control check and confirm the associated customer results cannot be reported until a named person dispositions it, and that the nonconforming work record carries its risk level, impact analysis and recall.

**Risk if skipped:** the accreditation-related rules on symbols, scope and separate reports are breached in a way that is visible on printed output; statements of conformity are made with no recorded decision rule; and a failed control check does not stop the results it invalidates from being reported.

---

#### 26.7 Phase 5 — Outward facing (6–8 weeks)

**Included:** the customer portal (status, past reports, invoices, a new request, a share-for-verification link with expiry and an access log); notifications by in-application message, email and SMS with templates in English and Telugu and a delivery log; the escalation ladder for overdue work; dashboards with no more than eight tiles; the analytics reports of §8 of the research brief — turnaround performance, bottleneck dwell time, first-time-right, rejection analysis, revenue per test and per customer, grade distribution by district and season, equipment utilisation; the retention and disposal register; the audit-trail extract; hardening of the public verification service, its accessibility conformance evidence, and its security review.

**What the laboratory can do at the end:** stop answering the telephone about status; see where the days actually go; and give headquarters trend data nobody could produce before.

**Acceptance milestone:** a real customer tracks a real sample and downloads a real report without telephoning the laboratory; and the accessibility and security reviews of the public page are closed.

**Risk if skipped:** the counter stays a call centre, and the genuine research value in five years of grade distributions by reeler and district is never realised.

---

#### 26.8 Phase 6 — Depth (5–7 weeks)

**Included:** instrument file import by watched folder, with a per-instrument mapping held as configuration, the raw file kept forever as an attachment with its fingerprint, and unmatched rows quarantined for a person; balance capture over a serial-to-USB adapter for high-volume weighing; worksheets and run sheets with quality-control positions; subcontracting with the customer's recorded approval and the identification of external results on the report; the stronger digital signature (an organisational Document Signer certificate on a hardware security module, swapped in behind the ARC-17 signing interface in place of the development key file, and producing a basic valid PAdES signature — **not** long-term validation, which the OPEN-Q-T31 default puts out of scope, and which if it is ever required arrives as a replacement signing implementation rather than as an addition to this one); the section 63 evidence certificate generator; the machine-readable report file alongside the PDF, so that a later DigiLocker onboarding is a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild; and second-unit readiness testing.

**Acceptance milestone:** 100 balance readings arrive from the instrument's own file with no typing, and the resulting report validates as digitally signed in an ordinary PDF reader with its tagged structure still intact after signing.

**Risk if skipped:** none that is urgent. **This is deliberately last.** Laboratories that begin with instrument interfacing spend the whole budget on three instruments and never ship the workflow. Many of this unit's tests — seriplane evenness, cleanness and neatness, cohesion counting, visual and tactual examination — are judgement against standard photographs with no digital output at all, so structured manual entry is the correct model for a large share of the work, not a compromise.

---

#### 26.10 Cut-over day

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **PLN-13** | Cut-over happens on a **stated date at a stated time**, agreed at least three weeks in advance, ideally the first working day of a month and preferably the first working day of a financial year so the number series start cleanly. The steps: (1) close the paper register at end of business on the last day, and rule a line in it with the date and the words "continued in the laboratory information system from tomorrow", signed by the Unit Incharge; (2) over the closed weekend, key in every open sample in its current state, with its true original receipt date and time; (3) count the consumable stock physically and enter opening balances; (4) enter opening unpaid invoices; (5) take a full backup; (6) print the opening sample register from the system and file it against the closed paper register. [MUST] |
| **PLN-14** | On cut-over day the developer is **physically present at the unit**, for the whole day. Not on a telephone. [MUST] |
| **PLN-15** | A written rollback decision point exists: if by 14:00 on cut-over day the counter cannot register samples, revert to paper for the day, record why, and reschedule. Deciding this in advance, calmly, is what stops a bad morning becoming a lost project. [MUST] |

#### 26.11 Parallel running with the paper system

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **PLN-16** | **Parallel running lasts four weeks, and it is deliberately asymmetric.** In weeks 1 and 2 the system is the primary record and the paper register is maintained as a **backup only** — written up at end of day from the system's own register printout, not maintained independently. In weeks 3 and 4 only the system is used, and the day's register is printed and filed. From week 5 the paper register is discontinued for new work and preserved as an archive. [MUST] |
| **PLN-17** | **Nobody keeps a parallel spreadsheet.** The reason a parallel record is fatal is that within a month the two disagree, and the moment they disagree the staff trust the paper and the system's data goes stale. If a member of staff needs something the system cannot give, that is a defect to be fixed in days, not a reason to open Excel. This must be said out loud by the Unit Incharge, to the staff, on cut-over day. [MUST] |
| **PLN-18** | The printed fallback forms of NFR-36 remain available permanently, with a written rule: if the system is unavailable, work continues on paper, and every paper entry is keyed in within one working day of the system returning, recording the true observation date and time and a reason for the late entry. [MUST] |
| **PLN-19** | For the first four weeks, the developer provides a same-day response to any defect reported by the laboratory, and a daily 15-minute call. Adoption is won or lost in the first fortnight. [MUST] |

### 27. Acceptance criteria and test scenarios

These are the tests that decide whether the system is accepted. Each is tagged with who runs it: **[LAB]** a member of the laboratory staff, unaided, following the scenario as written; **[DEV+LAB]** the developer sets up or operates the technical step while a named laboratory officer observes and signs the result; **[DEV]** the developer runs it and files a written test report that the Unit Incharge signs. The tags follow the allocation in §26.12. Only the criteria that need the developer carry a tag in the identifier column; **every untagged criterion is [LAB]**. Every one must be recorded as passed, failed, or passed-with-observation, and the completed set forms part of the software validation package required by ISO/IEC 17025 clause 7.11.2.

**Note on the "Verifies" column.** Where a requirement belongs to this section it is given by its identifier (NFR-, ARC-, DB-, PLN-). Where it belongs to a functional section written elsewhere in this document, the module is named in words rather than guessed at by number, so that the identifiers in this table are always correct.

#### 27.1 Happy path

| ID | Given | When | Then | Verifies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AC-01** | A trained front-desk clerk, a customer standing at the counter with 5 skeins of raw silk marked 20/22 denier, and no existing customer record | The clerk creates the customer, registers one sample, records the declared denier as a range, accepts the sample after the condition checklist, and prints the label | The whole action completes in under 3 minutes; the sample has a unique number; the label carries the number, sample type, received date, due date, test codes, a QR code and a barcode, **and no customer name**; a chain-of-custody "received" event exists | NFR-01, NFR-05, NFR-19, NFR-83, NFR-58; Sample registration, Labelling |
| **AC-02** | An intake of 30 lots of the same test for the same customer on one intake sheet | The clerk registers all 30 in one batch action | 30 sample numbers are allotted with no gaps and no duplicates; 30 tests are created; 30 labels queue; the batch completes in under 12 minutes total and under 10 seconds for the system's part | NFR-02, NFR-09, NFR-18, DB-08; Batch intake |
| **AC-03** | An accepted sample with one Limited Test allocated to an authorised tester, using an instrument in calibration | The tester scans the label at the bench, enters 20 readings using only the keyboard, and submits | The result-entry screen opens directly from the scan; the cursor advances automatically after each reading; the mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation and maximum deviation are computed; the submit completes in under 2 seconds; the tester can no longer edit the readings | NFR-03, NFR-04, NFR-14, NFR-78, NFR-41; Result entry |
| **AC-04** | A submitted test result | The Unit Incharge opens it, reviews it and verifies it | An electronic signature record is written with the signer, role, authorisation basis, time and address; the test moves to verified; the result becomes ready to report | NFR-102, DB-28; Verification |
| **AC-05** | A verified test on a sample | The Unit Incharge issues the report | A report number is allotted at that moment. A Unique Laboratory Report number is allotted **only** where the unit is configured as accredited and every parameter on the report is inside the accredited scope on that date; the unit is configured as accredited on certificate NABLT0726AD18713 (OPEN-Q-B12), so the number is allotted in the 26-character format whenever every parameter is in scope on that date, and is withheld — with no gap left in the series — whenever any parameter is not. The PDF is rendered, stored, fingerprinted and signed; the QR code resolves; the sample moves to reported; the report prints correctly on A4; every page carries the report number, the Unique Laboratory Report number **where one has been allotted**, and "page m of n"; the last page carries an end-of-report marker | NFR-16, NFR-39, NFR-42, NFR-79, DB-13, DB-26, DB-27; Report generation; Accredited scope and reporting |
| **AC-06** | An issued report in the hand of a buyer at the cocoon market | The buyer scans the QR code with an ordinary phone camera | The verification page opens; the banner reads GENUINE — VALID with an icon and words, not colour alone; the report number, date, issuing unit, sample description and status are shown; **the customer's name is masked or absent**; the file fingerprint is shown; the page is readable on a mid-range phone | ARC-18 to ARC-22, NFR-64, NFR-68, NFR-69, NFR-76; Public verification |

| **AC-07** [DEV+LAB] | A tester logged in, viewing a result-entry screen for a sample belonging to a named firm | The developer opens the browser's developer tools and inspects the raw data the server sent; the Unit Incharge observes and signs the result | The response **physically does not contain** the customer name, address, telephone number, tax registration number, price or invoice reference. It contains the sample number, sample type, description, declared values, test, method, parameters and due date | NFR-58; Confidentiality / blinding |
| **AC-08** | A tester needs to clarify an ambiguous bale mark | The tester requests unmasking, choosing a reason from the list, and the Unit Incharge approves | The reveal is limited to that one sample, expires after the configured period, and is written to the audit trail with who asked, who approved, when and why | NFR-102; Confidentiality / blinding |
| **AC-09** | A tester's account | The tester attempts to open the invoice screen, the rate card, and another tester's queue, by typing the address directly | All three are refused by the server, and each refusal is logged | NFR-58, ARC-11; Roles and permissions |
| **AC-10** | Two staff members sharing a workstation | Staff attempt to use one login for both | Not possible to satisfy the test: the account list contains no shared account, every screen shows the logged-in person's name, and the Unit Incharge has signed the account review confirming one account per person | NFR-47 |

#### 27.3 Unhappy paths — samples and work

| ID | Given | When | Then | Verifies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AC-11** | A sample arrives wet, with a torn wrapper, and 4 skeins instead of the 5 declared | The clerk records the condition, photographs it, and rejects the sample choosing a coded reason | The sample is in the rejected state with the reason, the photograph and the shortfall recorded; **no tests are created**; the customer intimation is logged; the sample is not deleted and remains in the register and the monthly counts | Sample acceptance and rejection; NFR-102, DB-02 |
| **AC-12** | A sample whose suitability is doubtful, where the customer insists on testing | The Unit Incharge accepts it with a deviation after recording the customer consultation | The sample proceeds; the deviation disclaimer is stored; **the disclaimer prints automatically on the report naming which results may be affected**; the report cannot be issued without it | Sample acceptance; Report content |
| **AC-13** | A submitted result with a transcription error in reading 7 | The verifier sends it back with a coded reason | The test returns to in-test; the retest count increases by one; the previous result values are archived and remain visible; the tester is notified; **the turnaround clock keeps running**; the tester can correct reading 7 by adding a superseding observation with a reason, leaving the original visible | DB-06, DB-33, NFR-104; Verification send-back |
| **AC-14** | A tester who is not authorised for the Grading method | The section head attempts to allocate a grading test to that tester, and then the tester attempts to enter a result directly | Both are refused with a plain message naming the missing authorisation; both refusals are logged; the override, if used, requires an authorised person, a reason, and opens a nonconforming work record | DB-32; Competency matrix |
| **AC-15** | A sample destroyed during a destructive test | A customer requests a retest on the retained material | The system reports that the material was consumed, showing the quantity consumed and the destroyed flag, rather than accepting a request the laboratory cannot fulfil | Sample lifecycle |
| **AC-16** | A test on hold for three working days awaiting a customer clarification | The hold is released and the report is later issued | The due date has moved forward by the hold duration; the report is **not** counted as a turnaround breach; the gross turnaround and the net laboratory turnaround are both reported and differ by three days | Turnaround; DB-15 |

#### 27.4 Unhappy paths — equipment, reagents and quality control

| ID | Given | When | Then | Verifies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AC-17** | A balance whose calibration expired 12 days ago, discovered today | A tester attempts to enter readings against that balance | Entry is refused, naming the instrument and the expiry date. If an authorised person overrides, a reason is mandatory and a nonconforming work record opens automatically | DB-30; Equipment control |
| **AC-18** | The same balance now fails its calibration, and the last known-good check was 40 days ago | The Unit Incharge records the failure and enters the suspect-from date | The system lists **every** test, sample and issued report that used that instrument in the window, in one action; each is dispositioned as not-affected with justification, retest, amend, or withdraw-and-replace; the dispositions are signed and dated; the instrument cannot return to service until a verification-before-service record exists | DB-20; Equipment impact analysis; Nonconforming work |
| **AC-19** | A reagent lot that expired last week, still physically on the shelf | A tester selects it during result entry | Selection is refused, evaluated **against the observation date, not today's date**; an override requires an authorised person and a reason and opens a nonconforming work record | DB-31; Consumable lots |
| **AC-20** | A daily control check that breaches its acceptance limit, run alongeight customer samples | The tester records the control result | The eight customer results in the same run are **automatically withheld from release**; no report can be issued for them until a named authorised person dispositions the breach; the withholding is visible on the queue with the reason | DB-42; Quality control |
| **AC-21** | Laboratory humidity recorded at 78% when the method requires 65 ± 2% | A tester attempts to submit a tenacity result observed during that period | The system warns, records the out-of-band environment against the test, and requires a decision from an authorised person before the result can be verified | Environment control |

| ID | Given | When | Then | Verifies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AC-22** | An issued report with a wrong customer address | The Unit Incharge issues a replacement report with a reason chosen from the list | A new report number is allotted; the new report states that it supersedes the original, naming its number and date; a machine-generated list of what changed is stored and printable; the original remains retrievable, unchanged, watermarked SUPERSEDED; a nonconforming work record opens unless the reason code is classified as non-nonconforming; the customer notification is logged | DB-07, DB-25; Report amendment |
| **AC-23** | The QR code on the **superseded** original, already in a trader's file | A buyer scans that original QR code | The page returns **GENUINE — SUPERSEDED**, naming the replacement report number and date, not a "page not found" and not the old content as if it were current. It never returns an error, because an error lets a forger claim the server is down | ARC-20; Public verification |
| **AC-24** | An issued report that must be withdrawn because it was issued against the wrong sample | The Unit Incharge withdraws it | The report state becomes withdrawn; the QR page shows GENUINE — WITHDRAWN with the date; a recall record names the customer, the notification channel and time; a nonconforming work record opens | Report withdrawal; Nonconforming work |
| **AC-25** | A genuine QR code photographed from a real report and pasted onto a doctored PDF | The recipient scans it and then uses the "check my PDF" control to upload their copy | The signature verifies but the page reports **"the document you uploaded does not match this QR code"**, naming the expected fingerprint | ARC-21, NFR-42; Public verification |
| **AC-26** | An order mixing one accredited parameter and one parameter outside the accredited scope | The Unit Incharge issues the report | The system produces **two** reports: one accredited, carrying the symbol and the Unique Laboratory Report number, and one non-accredited, carrying neither and making no accreditation claim. **No asterisk or footnote marker is used to distinguish scope on the accredited report.** Neither report hints at the other's accreditation status | DB-27; Accredited scope and reporting |
| **AC-50** | The unit configured as **accredited** on certificate `NABLT0726AD18713`, valid 17/07/2026 to 16/07/2030 (OPEN-Q-B12), with a test whose scope flag is **not yet set** because the scope annexure is not loaded (OPEN-Q-B12a) | A report is issued for that test | No accreditation symbol and no Unique Laboratory Report number appear anywhere on the report or its attachments, and no wording implies accredited status — an unset scope flag is treated as out of scope, never as in scope | DB-27; Accredited scope and reporting |
| **AC-50a** | The same unit, with a test whose scope flag **is** set from the loaded scope annexure | A report is issued for that test | The accreditation symbol prints, and the Unique Laboratory Report number prints in the 26-character form `NABLT0726AD18713` + report year + eight-digit running number, the running number being the next in that calendar year's gap-free series | WF-107, M8-35; Accredited scope and reporting |
| **AC-50b** | The same unit, with the system date advanced past 16/07/2030 and the accreditation not renewed | A report is issued for a test that is inside the accredited scope | The symbol and the Unique Laboratory Report number are suppressed automatically, without anyone having to remember to switch them off, and the report makes no accreditation claim | M8-35; Accredited scope and reporting |
| **AC-27** [DEV+LAB] | An issued report, its stored file, and a person with access to the server's disk | The developer alters one byte of the stored PDF on disk, then the Unit Incharge presses **"Run integrity check now"** on the administrator screen | The mismatch is reported immediately, naming the report; the file is refused to every requester; an alert is raised; a nonconforming work record opens. That the same check also runs weekly, unattended, is confirmed separately from the job log rather than by waiting seven days | NFR-42 |
| **AC-28** [DEV+LAB] | An issued report, six months old | Anyone attempts to change it through the application, and then the developer attempts the same change through a direct database statement while the Unit Incharge observes | The application refuses; the direct statement is refused by the database because the application login has no permission and the trigger blocks it; both attempts appear in the audit trail | NFR-43, DB-25, DB-04 |
| **AC-49** | A draft report compiled over a verified allocation and submitted for authorisation | The Unit Incharge retracts that allocation to In Test, the tester revises a reading, and the report is then submitted for authorisation again without being recompiled | The retraction returns the report to Draft and marks its snapshot stale, names the report number to the retracting user, and notifies the report writer and the signatory; authorisation and issue are both refused, naming the offending allocation and the report number, until the report is recompiled; no numbered, signed certificate is ever produced carrying the superseded value | DB-43, DB-21; Report compilation and authorisation |
